name: minipro
desc: Open controller for the MiniPRO TL866xx series of chip programmers
why: Open driver for TL866 chip programmers, opening up EEPROM and microcontroller dumping with real hardware in hand.

brief.what_it_is: minipro is an open source command-line program that controls XGecu's TL866xx series of chip programmers (the MiniPRO hardware). The README says it runs on Linux, macOS and other Unix-like systems, and supports the TL866CS, TL866A, TL866II+, T48 and T56 programmers. You name a target device with -p and a file with -w (write) or -r (read). The README claims more than 13000 target devices, including AVRs, PICs, BIOS chips and EEPROMs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says XGecu does not provide a program for Linux or other Unix flavors, so the maintainers wanted a simple, free, open-source program with a command-line interface that could also sit under a GUI front-end if desired.

commands_seen.context: Synopsis: writes atmega48.bin to an ATMEGA48 target chip.

brief.install_notes: Needs libusb 1.0.16 or newer. Linux build dependencies are listed per distro (Debian/Ubuntu, CentOS 7, openSUSE, Fedora), e.g. libusb-1.0-0-dev and zlib1g-dev on Debian. Clone from GitLab, then make and sudo make install. For regular-user access, install the udev rules and add your user to plugdev, then log out and back in. Bash completion is optional (bash_completion.d/minipro). Packaging is covered for .deb, PPA source packages, and .rpm for Fedora, CentOS and openSUSE. Guix users can run guix install minipro. On macOS, Homebrew is easiest; compiling from source needs pkg-config and libusb from brew or MacPorts. T56 users need the make algorithm step to fetch Xgecu's bitstreams.
brief.standout: The T56 does not keep its FPGA bitstreams in the hardware, so the host software has to load them. The project cannot ship those for copyright reasons, so its build downloads them from XGecu's official package and converts them into one file. The README also notes that GitLab tarball hashes are unstable, and points packagers to the FreeBSD ports approach of pinning a commit hash.
brief.status: unknown. The README names 0.7.4 as the latest 'stable' version, but it gives no release date. The GitLab page shows only a creation date of June 02, 2018, and no last-commit or release date was visible to me. The README also links an active FreeBSD port, which suggests ongoing packaging, but that is not proof of recent activity.
brief.caveats: Tested on Linux and macOS only; other Unices may work but are untested. libusb older than 1.0.16 is untested. T56 support needs Xgecu's algorithms, which the project cannot distribute, so you must run the download step yourself. License is GNU GPLv3 per the GitLab page. The Guix udev snippet in the README appears truncated (unclosed parenthesis). The scout notes list a dump-alg-minipro.bash executable, which I did not see described in the README.
quotes: This program exists because XGecu does not provide a program for use on Linux or other flavors of Unix.
